messages:
maria: Heads-up — started seeing p95 spike on hosted regions after the kernel-vecpath rollout (~2h ago). Looks correlated with long sequences and heavy KV traffic. Anyone else?

tyler: Yep, noticed it on canary and a few prod boxes. GPU mem climbs steadily, then we hit a few OOMs and recover. Tail latency jumps around the same time.

alex: I ran a quick profile across the canary fleet. Fragmentation numbers and allocator churn are much higher than baseline. KV slab utilization dropped even though total entries stayed ~constant. Paste from profiler:
```
KV cache: total=48GB slab_count=120 fragmented=6.2GB (13%)
workspace: avg_size=512KB -> 1.8MB under stress
alloc_calls/sec: +120%
decode-prefill ratio: decode-heavy (prefill rate ~0.18)
kv_hit_rate: 0.71 -> 0.63 during spike windows
kernel-switches/sec: +45% (fallbacks to vec-slow)
```

sam: My hypothesis: the kernel change reduced memory density for certain shapes, increasing per-request workspace. That + aggressive prefill sizes means more small allocations littering slabs -> fragmentation. Two levers to try: lower per-request prefill cap, and increase free-list coalescing frequency.

maria: I can try a quick canary change. Proposed immediate toggles: `prefill.per_request_cap=2MB` (was 8MB), `slab.compact_threshold=0.6` -> force compaction at higher fragmentation, and `workspace.reuse=true`.

infra-bot: deploybot: rollout started to canary nodes (region-us-west-2) — change set: prefill.cap=2MB, slab.compact=0.6, workspace.reuse=on.

benchmark-bot: quick 30m canary summary: p95 reduced 540ms -> 380ms, p50 ~ stable, OOMs 3 -> 0 in last 30m, but observed throughput down ~4% for seq>1024 workloads.

tyler: Positive on tail and OOMs, but the throughput hit worries me. I think kernel routing is falling back to a lower-throughput kernel with smaller memory footprint for some batches. We should bias routing to prefer lower-memory kernel only when workspace delta > X.

alex: Also seeing that small persistent free chunks (~4–16KB) accumulate in slabs. Free-list coalescing only runs at 200ms windows; if we drop it to 50ms we reduce fragmentation at the cost of a bit more CPU overhead on the allocator. Proposed: `free_coalesce_window_ms=50`.

maria: Can someone run a targeted memstress with the current canary flags? Command I use: `./memstress --kv-sim --seq-dist long --batch 64 --duration 10m --trace allocs`

tyler: Running now on canary-3, will paste condensed logs.

tyler: log snippet:
```
00:00 alloc_total=24GB frag=12% active_slabs=98
00:05 alloc_total=28GB frag=16% active_slabs=106
00:10 alloc_total=34GB frag=21% active_slabs=114
00:12 decode_concurrency spikes from 12 -> 24, kernel-fallbacks +60%
00:15 alloc_total=38GB frag=22% active_slabs=120
```

alex: Thanks. That curve matches allocator churn from excessive small allocations. Two-phase plan: short-term (canary) = reduce prefill cap + enable reuse + tighter coalesce window; medium-term = implement slab compaction pass that coalesces on-demand during low-util windows and a new eviction priority that considers reuse-cost.

sam: For eviction scoring: idea is to bias evicting prefill entries when decode reuse probability is low. Rough sketch: `evict_score = base_age * (1 + prefill_bias * is_prefill) * (1 - reuse_prob)` with `prefill_bias ~ 0.5` on canary. That should reduce prefill pressure while preserving decode caches.

maria: Caveat — chat multi-turn paths rely on prefill to avoid re-prefill cost. Aggressive prefill eviction could regress quality for those routes. So keep the bias limited to canary routes (non-chat; reranking/long-seq batch paths).

benchmark-bot: ran a short synthetic: with `free_coalesce_window_ms=50` + `prefill.cap=2MB` + `workspace.reuse=true`: fragmentation dropped from 22% -> 11% in 20m; p95 improved but long-seq throughput -3.8%.

tyler: Next steps from my side: open perf card with test matrix (prefill caps [1MB,2MB,4MB], coalesce window [50,100,200ms], kernel routing thresholds [seq>512, >1024]) and include eviction bias toggle. I'll tag infra and perf.

alex: I'll prototype an on-demand slab compactor that triggers when free_ratio < 0.15 for > 30s and runs a best-effort merge. Low-priority thread, yields on high CPU.

maria: Sounds good. For immediate prod safety, I'll keep the canary changes running and monitor kv_hit_rate and p95. Ping me if you see p95 creep back up. :thumbsup:

sam: One more note — we should gather a metric: per-request allocated_bytes (over lifetime) and correlate with kernel selected. That will help decide routing policy thresholds.

tyler: Agreed. I'll add that to the perf card. Attaching the canary run link in the perf card once created.

maria: Thanks team — good triage. We'll iterate on eviction bias + compacting approach and keep monitoring.
